text:
maria: noticing a sustained apiserver p95 jump in eu-west1 for the last 6m, controller-manager reconcile queue growing fast :grimacing:

sre-bot: alert: apiserver_high_latency - eu-west1 - triggered at 2923456778

ajay: I see large etcd compaction tasks around the same time. compact job started ~2923456740 per logs.

maria: here are the apiserver traces, looks like many list/watch requests are stalling during compaction windows:
```
E0320 12:26:10.123 apiserver.go:456] long-running request: 200ms default watch handler, k8s.io/..., resourceVersion: 3523442
etcd 2026-03-20 12:26:08.987 compact scheduled range [0,3523442] took 1.8s
```

jin: controller-manager showing backlog: pods pending controller processing ~1200, node-add events queued. autoscaler probes failing to reconcile GPU pools.

liz: so this is impacting GPU provisioning? we just had a burst of spot node attachments in eu-west1 and the cluster's not processing adds. potential customer impact for dedicated customers. :eyes:

kevin: can we confirm etcd disk IO at the time? compaction + snap save can cause read amplification.

ajay: checking iostat on etcd hosts now — saw short iowait spikes to 40%. also leader was on a machine in the overloaded rack.

maria: quick mitigation ideas: 1) pause scheduled compactions for 30m, 2) scale apiserver replicas to absorb stalls, 3) move etcd leader to a healthier replica. thoughts?

jin: +1 to moving leader. we can use etcdctl migrate-leader or demote the current leader. also scale controller-manager horizontally (2->4) for short term.

ajay: command to transfer leader:
```
etcdctl --endpoints=https://10.1.2.3:2379 member list
etcdctl --endpoints=https://10.1.2.3:2379 migrate-leader <target-member-id>
```

liz: if we scale apiserver, watch cache spikes might increase mem pressure. do we have headroom in eu-west1 control plane?

kevin: we have 2 spare apiserver nodes in that region tag pool. I can spin them up and roll a new replica.

maria: action: ajay to migrate leader + check disk IO, kevin to scale apiserver replicas, jin to scale controller-manager and throttle autoscaler sync period to reduce churn. I'll update on customer impact.

ajay: leader moved to member-id 7f9c3, I/O dropped from 40% -> 12% within two minutes. compaction still running but less impact.

kevin: apiserver scaled + rolled, p95 latency improving from 850ms -> 160ms.

jin: controller-manager replicas 2->4, set --horizontal-sync-period to 30s (was 5s) temporarily. reconcile backlog decreasing.

maria: nice. GPU autoscaler probes started succeeding again, we saw 80% of pending nodes attach succeed in the last 3m.

liz: customer-facing note: I'm drafting a short incident update for affected Dedicated accounts in eu-west1, include that we had control-plane latency during compaction window and we've applied mitigations.

kevin: one follow-up: we should change compaction scheduling to avoid peak provisioning hours. maybe use randomized jitter and a longer compaction window.

ajay: agree. also filing ops task to add ioops headroom alarms for etcd nodes and to ensure leader prefers high-io replicas.

maria: retrospective actions: document compaction timing, add a runbook step to check leader placement before heavy provisioning, add a controller-manager tuning doc for autoscaler-friendly settings.

jin: small note on cost: scaling apiserver/controller temporarily increased CPU by ~1.6 vCPU-region for 10m, cost negligible vs customer impact. logging that in the incident ticket.

maria: closing loop: latency stable, controller backlog drained. opening follow-up ticket SRE-3421 for compaction schedule + leader affinity. thanks everyone :thumbsup:

sre-bot: incident resolved: apiserver_high_latency - eu-west1 - resolved at 2923456905
